dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin.
Morning, Kevin. Alan Tillinghast here. I'm going to apologize in advance, because I'm standing at a gas station next to a pump, so if you hear a clunk, that's me getting old and leaning on things.
No problem, I can hear you fine. What can I do for you, Alan?

Well, I've got a drain issue. A storm drain grate at the curb, it's sunk. Dropped down below the pavement, and now when it rains the water goes everywhere but down the thing. It's very talented water, I'll give it that.
Okay. Sunken grate, water's bypassing it. Where is this at?
69 Memorial Boulevard. That's the Easton's Beach side, across from the beach, up toward the end where it bends a little.
Got it, 69 Memorial Boulevard. And when did you notice it? Was this from the rain over the weekend?

Yeah, the rain Friday and Saturday, two days ago. I own the building, I'm the landlord, so I went by Sunday to check on things. The water had pooled up along the curb and run across, and it left the sidewalk a sheet of mud and grit. Just a layer of silt, you could write your name in it.
Okay, so sediment all over the sidewalk in front of the property. Is the water getting up onto the property itself, or is it staying out on the street and sidewalk?
Mostly the street and sidewalk. It runs along the edge and spreads out wide before it finds anywhere to go. Nothing inside, I checked.
Good. And the grate itself, is it the metal grate that's sunk, or is the pavement around it settling?

The whole thing, I think. The grate sits lower than the road now, like the frame went down and took a bite of asphalt with it. And there's a dip around it, but the water skirts around the dip instead of going in. Physics doing its own thing.

Yeah, that happens. Frames settle, or the catch basin underneath shifts. I'll write it up as a sunken catch basin grate, possible settling, with silt on the sidewalk. Is it blocked with debris too, do you know?
Some leaves and sand on top, but I don't think that's the real problem. It's the sinking.
Okay. Let me get that down. Sunken grate, 69 Memorial Boulevard, drainage bypassing it after the Friday and Saturday rain. Do you want a call back when it gets scheduled, or just want it on the list?
A call back would be fine. I'm at 401-555-0163.
Okay, 401-555-0163, under Tillinghast. T-I-L-L-I-N-G-H-A-S-T, right?
You got it. Rhode Island's finest spelling test.
I do it every day. All right, I'll send this over to the crew that handles drains and catch basins. They'll look at it and figure out whether it's a reset of the frame or something bigger underneath.
Makes sense. Can I ask, do the crews work weekends? Because if it's going to rain again I'd like to know someone might get to it before then.

Weekends are mostly for emergencies, like a road that's flooded out or something dangerous. A sunken grate with water running past it would normally get handled on a weekday. After a storm they've got a pile of these, so it could be a few days to a couple of weeks.
Okay. That's about what I figured. I'm not asking anyone to come out in a canoe.
No canoes needed. If it gets worse, like if the water starts coming up toward the building or the road is covered, call us right back and I'll mark it urgent.
Will do. And the mud on the sidewalk, is that something the city cleans or is that on me?

Usually if the crew is out there fixing the basin they'll clear what's around it. I'll note the silt on the sidewalk in the ticket so they see it. Beyond that, the sidewalk in front of a building is typically the owner's to sweep, so you might want to give it a go once the drain's working so it doesn't just wash back.
Fair enough. No sense sweeping it if it's going to refill. I'll wait.
Yeah, that's smart. All right, I've got everything. Sunken grate, 69 Memorial Boulevard, call back at 401-555-0163. Anything else?
That's it. Thanks, Kevin. I'll let you get back to it.
Thanks for calling, Alan. Take care, and watch the pump.
Will do. Bye now.
